top_temples.name: Buddha Temple (Gompa Buddhist Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Atop a hill in Itanagar; a Tibetan-influenced temple with a stupa in front, offering panoramic views of the city.

top_temples.name: Ganga Jamuna Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Itanagar; a Hindu temple dedicated to the sacred rivers.

top_temples.name: Karuwabasti Bodo Bathou Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Itanagar; established by the Bodo community, dedicated to Bathouism.

top_temples.name: Sri Sri Radha Krishna Mandir, Itanagar
top_temples.location_note: Itanagar; a Vaishnavite temple offering a space for prayer and community gathering.

top_temples.name: Shiv Mandir, Itanagar
top_temples.location_note: Itanagar.

top_temples.name: Bomdila Monastery (Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Ling / GRL, Upper Gompa)
top_temples.location_note: Bomdila, West Kameng district; built 1965-66 inspired by South Tibet's Tsona Gontse Monastery, sanctified by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1997.

top_temples.name: Lower Gompa, Bomdila
top_temples.location_note: At the edge of Bomdila's main market area, one of the monastery's three divisions along with the Middle and Upper Gompa, known for its Tibetan architecture and prayer hall.

top_temples.name: Malinithan Temple Ruins
top_temples.deity: Krishna, Rukmini, Shiva, and Parvati (per associated legend)
top_temples.location_note: On a hill at the base of the Siang mountains, Likabali, Lower Siang district; early medieval Hindu temple ruins dated to the 13th-15th centuries, built in classical Odisha style, with a new replica temple and excavation display gallery.

top_temples.name: Akashiganga Temple
top_temples.deity: Shakti (Sati, as the site of her head)
top_temples.location_note: About 12 km from Malinithan towards Along, West Siang district; a revered Shakti pilgrimage site with a sacred kund 100 metres from the temple.

top_temples.name: Naharlagun Buddhist Temple (Thupsung Dhargye Ling)
top_temples.location_note: Naharlagun, Papum Pare district; built in Tibetan architectural style.

top_temples.name: Digambar Jain Temple (Bh. Parshwanath)
top_temples.location_note: Naharlagun; built by the local Jain community, with a finely carved inner sanctum and religious library.

top_temples.name: Parshuram Kund
top_temples.location_note: On the Lohit River in Lohit district, about 21 km north of Tezu; Parasuram Kund's central and defining shrine, site of the annual Makar Sankranti Parashuram Mela drawing over 70,000 pilgrims.

top_temples.name: Devi Renuka Shrine
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Parasuram Kund temple complex as the main Parshuram shrine, alongside a Dashavatar temple to Vishnu's ten incarnations.

top_temples.name: Bongkud Monying
top_temples.location_note: A hillock shrine overlooking Pasighat town and the Siang river valley; devotees trek up to perform puja.

top_temples.name: Dangaria Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Pasighat town; established per local folklore dating to 1962.

top_temples.name: Kupunli Cave Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Hunli, about a 2-hour trek from Hunli town in the Roing area, Lower Dibang Valley district.

top_temples.name: Bhismaknagar Temple Complex
top_temples.deity: Associated with the Rukmini/Bhismak legend from the Mahabharata
top_temples.location_note: About 30 km from Roing, Lower Dibang Valley district; 8th-century archaeological ruins of fort walls and temple structures.

top_temples.name: Tawang Monastery
top_temples.location_note: Tawang town; the largest Buddhist monastery in India, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso, giving the town its defining religious identity.

top_temples.name: Tawang Taktshang Monastery
top_temples.location_note: About 45 km from Tawang township, within the same Tawang district; a three-tiered site believed consecrated by Guru Padmasambhava in the 8th century.

top_temples.name: Temple (Tezu Temple-Monastery-Gurudwara Compound)
top_temples.deity: Hindu worship (specific deity/name not independently documented)
top_temples.location_note: Tezu, Lohit district headquarters; a Hindu temple standing alongside a Buddhist monastery and a Sikh gurudwara in the same shared compound, reflecting the town's multi-faith character. No second distinct temple could be verified for Tezu despite repeated searches; this entry lists only one temple.

top_temples.name: Shree Siddheshwar Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kardo Forest, Ziro town, Lower Subansiri district, at 5,754 ft; houses the world's largest naturally formed Shiva Linga (about 25 ft above ground), discovered by a woodcutter in July 2004.

top_temples.name: Meghna Cave Temple
top_temples.location_note: A few kilometers from Ziro town, reached via a forested trek to about 300 ft altitude; an ancient cave shrine dated to roughly 5,000 years, discovered in 1962.
